v: This module assesses whether the paper's code could be run on its data, and — because `execute = TRUE` — **actually ran it**. We examined 1 R code file.
The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first), `source()` calls, and numeric filename prefixes.

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list(Order = 1L, File = "model_object.R", "Runs after" = "—", 
    Basis = "none"), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = "data.frame")

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 10, FALSE)
```
To run against the Psych-DS layout, 1 referenced data path would be rewritten to its new location.
Every data file the code reads is either produced by an earlier script or present in the repository.

**The code was run.** Each script ran in an isolated subprocess against a throwaway copy of the Psych-DS layout, in the run order above, with a 60-second per-script timeout. Of 1 script: 1 ran without error, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 were skipped (inputs unavailable), 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, and 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions.

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list(File = "model_object.R", Outcome = "ran_ok", Detail = "", 
    "Time (s)" = 0), row.names = c(NA, -1L), class = "data.frame")

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 15, FALSE)
```
